topics.title: The First World War and the idea of satyagraha

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the First World War created a new economic and political situation in India.
Explain the idea of satyagraha as active, non-violent resistance based on truth.
Identify Gandhiji's early satyagrahas at Champaran, Ahmedabad and Kheda and the groups they supported.

topics.title: The Rowlatt Act, Khilafat and the call for Non-Cooperation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Indians opposed the Rowlatt Act and how the Rowlatt satyagraha unfolded.
Describe the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the repression that followed.
Explain why Gandhiji joined the Khilafat issue to Non-Cooperation and how the movement was planned in stages.

topics.title: Differing strands within the Non-Cooperation Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Describe middle-class participation and the economic boycott in the towns, and why it slowed down.
Explain how peasants in Awadh and tribals in the Gudem Hills interpreted swaraj in their own ways.
Explain what freedom meant to Assam plantation workers under the Inland Emigration Act.

topics.title: Towards Civil Disobedience and the Salt March

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the withdrawal of Non-Cooperation, the Swaraj Party's council politics and the impact of the depression.
Describe the protests against the Simon Commission and the Lahore Congress demand for Purna Swaraj.
Explain why the Salt March was an effective symbol and how Civil Disobedience differed from Non-Cooperation.

topics.title: How participants saw Civil Disobedience and its limits

concepts.learning_objective: Compare why rich peasants, poor peasants, business classes, workers and women joined Civil Disobedience.
Explain the dalit demand for separate electorates and the outcome of the Poona Pact.
Analyse why large sections of Muslims felt alienated from the Congress-led movement.
Describe how the image of Bharat Mata came to symbolise the nation.
Explain how folklore revival and nationalist flags helped create a feeling of nationalism.
Evaluate how nationalist histories built pride in the past and why they could exclude some communities.
